boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named HWS spaces where students study, meet, make art, hold discussions, explore the grounds and participate in recreation.

cards.title: Settle In Above the Library’s Main Floor
cards.subtitle: A shared study hub with research and academic support nearby
cards.notes: Try the second floor for daylight and a view of Stern Lawn, then head downstairs when you need research, technology or learning support.
cards.short_summary: A central study setting that puts library, technology and academic-help services in one building.
cards.evidence_claim: HWS identifies Warren Hunting Smith Library as a place where students gather to study and conduct research; a 2025 campus photo feature documents a student studying on its second floor.
cards.access_notes: Library privileges and some services are reserved for current HWS community members; consult current library information before visiting.

cards.title: See What Student Curators Put on the Walls
cards.subtitle: A student-run gallery inside Scandling Campus Center
cards.notes: Walk through during posted gallery hours, or contact the gallery if your group wants to propose an exhibition, event or collaborative project.
cards.short_summary: Students select, install and promote exhibitions in this campus-center gallery.
cards.evidence_claim: HWS states that the Provenzano Student Art Gallery is student-run and that student interns collaboratively plan, design, install, coordinate and promote exhibitions and events.
cards.access_notes: The official page currently lists Monday-Friday 10 a.m.-6 p.m. and Saturday-Sunday noon-4 p.m.; contact the gallery for changes or event booking.

cards.title: Switch Between Conversation and Coursework
cards.subtitle: Student-designed commons for social time and study
cards.notes: Use the commons when your group needs a flexible meeting point with seating, then move to a quieter campus space if focused work takes over.
cards.short_summary: Reconfigured lounges and dining areas support both informal gathering and studying.
cards.evidence_claim: HWS describes the enhanced Scandling Campus Center as a student-designed commons whose lounges and dining areas accommodate social and study uses.
cards.access_notes: Campus-center spaces may be affected by dining operations, scheduled programs and college access rules; check current campus information.

cards.title: Bring an Idea to an Open Student Government Meeting
cards.subtitle: Coxe Hall event space for clubs, forums and campus programs
cards.notes: Attend an open student-government meeting to hear current campus issues, or work through Student Engagement when planning a club event here.
cards.short_summary: A former black-box theatre repurposed for student meetings and collective programs.
cards.evidence_claim: HWS says Bartlett Theatre is used for club meetings, celebrations, academic forums and campus events; 2026-27 student-government meetings are held there and are open to all HWS students.
cards.source_title: Hobart and William Smith Student Government
cards.access_notes: The official page lists student-government meetings during fall and spring classes on Mondays at 8 p.m.; agendas are distributed to students.

cards.title: Take a Discussion Outside
cards.subtitle: A landscaped lecture space beside HWS classroom buildings
cards.notes: Suggest this named outdoor classroom when a seminar or study group benefits from fresh air; plan an indoor fallback for poor weather.
cards.short_summary: Built-in benches turn the campus landscape into a setting for classes and group discussion.
cards.evidence_claim: HWS states that the Classes of 1972 Outdoor Classroom has benches integrated into the landscape and is where faculty and students convene for discussion and critical thinking.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor academic space; avoid occupying it when a class or scheduled college activity is underway.

cards.title: Make Room for a Larger Dialogue
cards.subtitle: Gathering space in the Adams Intercultural Center
cards.notes: Watch for AIC forums and dialogues here, or coordinate with the center before proposing a group conversation that needs multipurpose space.
cards.short_summary: The AIC’s multipurpose room was created for larger groups to gather around discussion.
cards.evidence_claim: HWS documents the Stine Multipurpose Room as part of the Adams Intercultural Center expansion and says it provides space for large groups to gather for forums and dialogues.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to Adams Intercultural Center programming and room scheduling; contact the center before organizing an event.

cards.title: Use an Exhibition as Course Material
cards.subtitle: Academic gallery inside Houghton House
cards.notes: Visit during posted hours with a class question in mind; students in curatorial work also use the gallery to connect objects with academic theory.
cards.short_summary: An academic gallery where exhibitions and curatorial practice intersect with coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: HWS calls the Davis Gallery an academic resource and explains that students curate exhibitions there using objects from the Colleges’ art collection.
cards.access_notes: The official page currently lists Monday-Friday 9:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m., Saturday 1-3 p.m., or visits by appointment.

cards.title: Trade a Study Break for a Trail Walk
cards.subtitle: Campus woodland used for walking and field research
cards.notes: Follow established trails for a between-class reset, and leave research plots undisturbed when courses or student projects are collecting field data.
cards.short_summary: A named campus woodland that supports both trail walks and hands-on environmental study.
cards.evidence_claim: An HWS campus photo feature identifies trails in Coopers’ Woods as a place to take a break and walk; HWS also documents student forest-monitoring research there.
cards.access_notes: Use established paths in suitable weather and observe posted campus or research-area restrictions.

cards.title: Pause Between Arts-Campus Classes
cards.subtitle: A named library space at Houghton House
cards.notes: Use this quieter stop for reading or reflection between Houghton House and Elliott Studio Arts Center commitments, while respecting building access.
cards.short_summary: A reflective study option situated within HWS’s arts-campus setting.
cards.evidence_claim: HWS’s 2025 campus photo feature documents a student using Houghton House Library for introspection between classes there and at Elliott Studio Arts Center.
cards.access_notes: Access follows Houghton House and college schedules; confirm availability before relying on it as a study destination.

cards.title: Choose a Shared Way to Move
cards.subtitle: Home base for HWS recreation programs and facilities
cards.notes: Check the current recreation schedule, then choose among open recreation, group fitness or intramurals that match your eligibility and experience.
cards.short_summary: Indoor recreation facilities give students multiple ways to exercise alongside others.
cards.evidence_claim: HWS says its recreation programs predominantly operate in Bristol Field House, which contains a fitness and weight room, indoor track, courts and group-exercise spaces.
cards.access_notes: Facility eligibility, program registration and hours vary; consult the current HWS Recreation schedule and access requirements.
